sections.skill: Analyze how AI may change some tasks in a job

questions.prompt: What is a job made of?
questions.intro: A JOB is made of many TASKS. A medical receptionist, for example, schedules appointments, answers calls, comforts worried patients, handles insurance forms and solves surprise problems. AI may change SOME tasks, such as drafting reminder messages or filling forms, while others, such as calming an upset patient, change little. So "Will AI take this job?" is usually the wrong question. Better questions: Which tasks might AI help with or change? Which depend on judgment, trust, physical presence or responsibility? How might the job shift as a result? Changes can add new tasks, too, such as checking AI drafts.

sections.skill: Compare a job with a toolbox of tasks

questions.prompt: What does the power drill replace?

choices.text: Some uses of the hand screwdriver
The carpenter completely, since a drill can build an entire house without a person

questions.correct_answer: Some uses of the hand screwdriver
questions.intro: Think of a job as a TOOLBOX of tasks. A new power drill replaces the hand screwdriver for some jobs, but the hammer, tape measure and the carpenter's judgment are still needed, and now someone must know how to use the drill safely. The carpenter's job changed; it did not vanish. AI is like a new tool in the box: it changes some tasks, leaves others, and adds new ones.

questions.prompt: What is still needed?

sections.title: Apply it

questions.prompt: Tasks in a job could be automated, but the job changes slowly. What might explain this?

choices.text: Nothing explains it, since automation always happens immediately once it is possible

questions.intro: Task analysis has limits. A job whose tasks could be automated may still change slowly because of cost, rules, customer preferences or the need for someone to be responsible. A job might also shrink in some places and grow in others. Two simple predictions are both risky: "nothing will change" and "the whole job will disappear." Look at evidence over time, and notice that workers who learn to use and check new tools well often shape how their own jobs change.

questions.prompt: Which prediction is most reasonable?

choices.text: "This whole job will certainly disappear within one year, everywhere in the world."
"Nothing about this job will ever change."
"Some tasks will change; how much is uncertain."
"AI will do every job by next month."

questions.correct_answer: "Some tasks will change; how much is uncertain."
